title: Ensure AI Agents Work: Evaluation Frameworks for Scaling Success — Aparna Dhinkaran, CEO Arize
talk_summary: Aparna Dhinkaran argues agents should be evaluated at each trace component—router, skills, memory/path—not just final output, using code-based and LLM-judge evals. She shows Arize dogfooding live co-pilot traces with evals on overall response, router choice/arguments, and skill execution.

takeaways.what_they_do: Instrument each agent run as a trace and attach evals to router decisions, tool/skill execution, and final response so failures are localized to a layer.
takeaways.evidence_quote: evals aren't just at one layer of your entire Trace

takeaways.what_they_do: Evaluate whether the agent chose the correct next skill/tool and passed the correct arguments, not just whether the final answer looked right.
takeaways.evidence_quote: is it calling the right skill with the right parameters

takeaways.what_they_do: Measure how many steps/tool calls an agent takes to complete the same task and track variance across runs and models.
takeaways.evidence_quote: reliability in the number of steps that your agent takes to actually consistently complete a task

takeaways.what_they_do: Break a skill into component evals—retrieval relevance, answer correctness, code-based checks—instead of relying on one aggregate score.
takeaways.evidence_quote: correctness of the answer that was generated

takeaways.what_they_do: Evaluate the relevance of chunks pulled into context before generation, so irrelevant context can be pruned or re-retrieved.
takeaways.evidence_quote: evaluating the actual relevance of the chunks that were pulled

takeaways.what_they_do: Run evals on live production traces, not only offline test sets, and inspect real agent steps in the wild.
takeaways.evidence_quote: every single step of this co-pilot we actually run evaluations of
